The conflict remains open and unaddressed by this pass.

bias_observations: Name leakage into the 'blind' pass is direct and documented. The github modality's own query list includes `gh api orgs/nautechsystems/repos`, `gh api orgs/QuantConnect/repos`, `gh api orgs/alpacahq/repos` and `gh api orgs/quantopian/repos`, plus seeded searches 'nautilus trader stars:>50', 'lean algorithmic trading engine', 'zipline reloaded', 'backtrader' and 'vnpy rqalpha qlib pybroker backtesting framework github'; the web modality adds 'QuantConnect LEAN vs open source backtesting engines' and 'hummingbot freqtrade jesse nautilus trader comparison'. The pass therefore name-targeted the catalog's two selected engines and its selected broker org before ranking them 1st and 2nd. The convergence with the catalog on NautilusTrader/LEAN carries much less independent weight than an unseeded sweep would.

Star anchoring is explicit and the blind pass admits it. merit.limits records that 32 of 39 candidates passed every mechanical rule, exceeding the 12-repo cap, 'so stars ... was used as the tiebreak to select the final 12; this tiebreak is stated explicitly here since the task's rule set did not itself specify a secondary ordering'. The research judge then attacks that filter in its own limits: it admitted three crypto-only bots (freqtrade 54.6k, hummingbot 20.1k, jesse 8.6k) that score 0 on capability fit, while excluding stefan-jansen/zipline-reloaded (1,940 stars) which 'passes every mechanical rule except the star cut'. Lumibot (2,079 stars), the catalog's closest Python Alpaca-lifecycle alternative, was cut the same way and never judged.

Awesome-list echo chamber. The awesome modality mined four overlapping curated lists (wilsonfreitas/awesome-quant, paperswithbacktest/awesome-systematic-trading, georgezouq/awesome-ai-in-finance, wangzhe3224/awesome-systematic-trading) and reports that supplemental Tavily searches 'returned mostly low-signal blog/LinkedIn posts and the same awesome-list repos already covered'. One of the lists, wangzhe3224/awesome-systematic-trading, entered the merged candidate set as a repository and had to be dropped at the merit gate as 'not itself a backtest/simulation engine'. Two of the four lists are also already in the catalog (repository-index.md:337 and :463), so this modality partly re-derives the catalog's own sources.

Vendor-marketing evidence reached a top-ranked SOTA claim. The research judge sourced its NautilusTrader parity claim to https://nautilustrader.io/blog/why-nautilustrader-exists; the refuter confirmed the mechanism but only from docs/concepts/architecture.md, noting the judge cited 'a company marketing blog post, the weakest evidence class offered in either judge's set'. The refuter also stripped two overstatements in the same direction ('k-way' is the judge's word, not the docs'; determinism is conditional on random_seed; live.md itself says the live runner 'does not define one global FIFO order').

The blind pass acknowledges low-quality secondary web sources: 'Two of the python.financial and bullalert.ai sources read as SEO/possibly AI-generated comparison content rather than primary/authoritative sources'. Those same sources are cited in the merged NautilusTrader reasons as corroboration that it is 'the top pick for execution-mechanics fidelity'.

Mechanical license gating systematically favoured the wrong repos, and both judges had to correct it. NOASSERTION was treated as passing for StockSharp (proprietary EULA, verified LICENSE text), vectorbt (Apache-2.0 + Commons Clause), rqalpha (non-commercial only) and pybroker. This is a blind-pass bias toward permissive-looking metadata, and on vectorbt and pybroker the existing catalog records are demonstrably more accurate than the blind merit rows.

Catalog-side scope asymmetry, not bias but a systematic coverage mismatch. The catalog's engines-strategies layer carries 3 selected plus ~43 alternatives spanning engines, broker SDKs, portfolio optimizers, metrics libraries, econometrics and forecasting (scikit-learn, statsmodels, darts, chronos, timesfm). A sub-layer scoped to 'Backtest and simulation engines' can only ever cover a slice, and the blind web modality explicitly excluded quantstats/pyfolio/TA-Lib/cvxpy as 'adjacent tooling' - which are catalog Default/Alternative rows in the same layer. Coverage-diff percentages across this layer pair would be meaningless.

Catalog-side internal drift creates false disagreement signals. repository-index.md:289 still labels nautechsystems/nautilus_trader 'engines-strategies: alternative' while stack.json and the landscape json select it; repository-index.md:361 and engines-strategies.md:38 call lean-alpaca 'default' while the landscape json calls it 'conditional'. Any automated diff against those rows will report disagreements that are internal staleness, not evidence conflicts.
limits: No network verification was performed by me. Every star count, pushed_at, license field, release tag and CI-run tally in this report is the blind pass's recorded gh api output dated 2026-09-21/22, restated - not independently re-derived. The blind pass itself states that nothing was cloned, installed, built or executed and that 'fidelity' there means documented and code-visible features, not verified numerical correctness.

Presence/absence in the catalog was determined by literal case-normalised owner/repo matching plus bare repo-name matching over <PROJECTS_ROOT>/native-agent-stack-token-practice-review/catalogs/us-equities/*.md, manifests/stack.json and <PROJECTS_ROOT>/native-agent-stack-landscape-finalization-20260921/catalogs/landscape/*.json, followed by a repo-wide rg across both catalog repositories. A repository recorded only under an alias, a renamed org or a non-GitHub identifier could be missed. One false positive was caught and discarded: the only vnpy hit in the review repo is inside a base64 blob in docs/ecosystem/index.html, not a record.

I read the engines-strategies.md and repository-index.md tables, star-audit.md prose, decision-index.json and catalogs/us-equities/architecture/trading.json, but NOT engines-strategies.json or star-audit.json - the machine records those markdown rows link to. A disposition present only in those JSON files would not appear in this diff.

The two partial-coverage findings (hftbacktest, pybroker) turn on a structural question I could not settle from the supplied inputs: whether catalogs/us-equities/architecture/trading.json and decision-index.json are intended to feed the engines-strategies layer record. wf1-layers.json cites only engines-strategies.md, repository-index.md, catalogs/landscape/us-equities.json and manifests/stack.json, so I treated architecture/trading.json as out-of-band. If it is in scope, the correct action for both is no-action rather than add-candidate-row.

Both blind judges scored exactly the same 12 shortlisted repositories, so 'ranked' and 'shortlisted' are the same set here; the 27 merged candidates that never reached the merit shortlist were never judged, and I did not re-evaluate them beyond their merit metadata.

The refuter's better_alternatives_found is a set of three; I did not attempt to determine whether other unranked merged candidates (basana, hikyuu, qf-lib, barter-rs, investing-algorithm-framework, quantreplay, OctoBot, finmarketpy, zvt, optopsy, manifoldbt, aat, cloudQuant/backtrader, EigenLedger) warrant catalog rows, since none was shortlisted, ranked or refuter-promoted. pysystemtrade and manifoldbt do have metadata-only records in catalogs/us-equities/architecture/trading.json with decision 'not_adopted'.

The blind merged entry for pysystemtrade uses pst-group/pysystemtrade while its merit row resolved to robcarver17/pysystemtrade; the blind pass records this as a confirmed org transfer. I did not verify the redirect.

No acceptance command, count or exit code was derived by me. If a repo-wide grep count, a git log, or a re-run of the presence check against a different file set is needed as evidence, ask the coordinator to supply the command output.

bias_observations: Star-count anchoring is the dominant bias in the blind pass, and it is self-declared. merit.limits states: the four mechanical rules left 32 of 60 candidates passing against an 'at most 12' cap, 'No tiebreak rule was specified in the brief, so stars-descending ... was applied as the cutoff'. The named casualties are precisely the US-equities-relevant repositories: ib_async, alpaca-py, ib-gateway-docker, alpaca-trade-api-js/go, schwab-py, AmpyFin, lumibot, investing-algorithm-framework, omspy. judge0's limits state the consequence bluntly: 'Six of the twelve shortlisted repositories cannot reach any US-equities venue at all, so the mechanical star-ranked shortlist is biased toward crypto by construction.' The blind top-5 lists are therefore a ranking of survivors of a star filter, not of sub-layer fit.

Licence auto-detection produced a second mechanical bias: merit.limits records that StockSharp, the entire QuickFIX/QuickFIX-J/QuickFIX-Go/QuickFIX-n family, vectorbt, OpenBB, rqalpha and pybroker were dropped only because GitHub reports NOASSERTION/none, 'which can reflect a non-standard LICENSE format or dual/custom terms rather than an actual absence of licensing terms'. For StockSharp the refuter later read the LICENSE and the drop turned out correct; for the QuickFIX family (FIX protocol engines, directly on-topic for an OMS/execution sub-layer) no one checked, so an entire relevant class was removed by a metadata artefact.

Awesome-list echo chamber: the awesome modality contributed 24 candidates and its distinctive contributions are crypto-first engines (freqtrade, hummingbot, jesse, ccxt, blankly) plus already-dead projects (alpacahq/pylivetrader, last push 2022-10-04). Repos surfaced by all three modalities (nautilus_trader, Lean, ib_async, alpaca-py) are the same ones the catalog already holds, which suggests the three 'independent' modalities share upstream sources rather than being independent.

Name-leakage risk in the blind pass is present but does not look decisive. merit.limits asserts the BLINDNESS rule was honoured ('no file under <OPERATOR_HOME> was opened and no prior project selection (e.g. NautilusTrader/IBKR/Alpaca as "the" destination) was used'), yet the ability to name NautilusTrader/IBKR/Alpaca as the thing not to use shows the operator knew the catalog's destination. Mitigating evidence: nautilus_trader and Lean arrive via all three modalities at 29k/21k stars, alpaca-py was actually DROPPED by the mechanical tiebreak, and both judges scored Nautilus down on the Alpaca gap - behaviour inconsistent with anchoring on the catalog's answer.

The catalog's own audit is explicitly not blind, which limits how much independent confirmation the agreement on Nautilus/Lean can carry: star-audit.md:47 states 'These choices are conditioned on the existing LEAN research-first and Alpaca-paper direction.' Two conditioned processes converging on the same two engines is weaker evidence than it appears, and the one place the blind pass was genuinely unconditioned (Lumibot's in-core Alpaca/IBKR/Schwab adapters) is exactly where it disagrees with the catalog's ordering.

Asymmetric documentation on the catalog side: repository-index.md holds rows for repositories already inside the selection orbit (alpaca-py, lumibot, nautilus_trader, lean, lean.brokerages.alpaca) but records nothing at all for the seven crypto-first engines, thetagang, openalgo or barter-rs, and keeps hftbacktest and pysystemtrade only in architecture/trading.json. Exclusions are therefore invisible to any future sweep, which guarantees the same candidates keep reappearing as apparent gaps - and means 'absent from the catalog' conflates 'considered and rejected' with 'never seen'.

Evidence-class inflation risk on both sides: neither judge executed anything ('every 3 for evidence means abundant cited upstream artefacts, never a measured result I reproduced'), judge1's third-party search 'returned mostly low-quality secondary content (SEO blogs, social posts)', and has_tests/has_ci are directory-listing heuristics that both judges found wrong for ccxt, nautilus_trader and vnpy. OpenSSF Scorecard numbers (Nautilus 8.5 vs Lean 4.9 vs lumibot 5.5) are the one genuinely measured comparator in the set, and even there the refuter records the Code-Review sub-check at 1/10 - so it should not be used as a supply-chain ranking on its own.
limits: I executed no commands that produce acceptance evidence and verified no GitHub fact independently. Every star count, pushed_at, licence, release tag, issue number and OpenSSF score in this report is quoted from the blind pass's own gh api reads dated 2026-09-21/22 (with some pushed_at values reading 2026-09-22 UTC). Treat them as the blind worker's observations, not as re-verified data.

Catalog presence/absence was determined by recursive substring grep for repository names over <PROJECTS_ROOT>/native-agent-stack-token-practice-review and <PROJECTS_ROOT>/native-agent-stack-landscape-finalization-20260921 (excluding .git). A repository recorded under a different alias, org rename or spelling would be missed; conversely 'NONE' results for freqtrade, hummingbot, jesse-ai, openalgo, barter-rs, thetagang and StockSharp are whole-repo greps, so they are reliable for those exact strings only.

The blind shortlist is capped at 12 by a stars-descending tiebreak out of 32 rule-passing candidates, so roughly 20 candidates that passed every stated mechanical rule were never judged - including ib_async, alpaca-py, lumibot, schwab-py, ib-gateway-docker, ibeam, roboquant, investing-algorithm-framework and lean-cli. Any 'no blind modality surfaced' or 'blind found nothing better' conclusion is bounded by that cap.

neither judge ran code, installed anything, executed an upstream test suite or placed a paper order; runtime correctness, fill quality, latency, rate-limit behaviour and reconciliation-after-disconnect are unmeasured for all twelve shortlisted repositories. judge1 additionally states the Nautilus IB defect severity comes from issue titles only, with issue bodies unread and no check for a landed fix on a development branch - so the #4983 flag needs the issue body read before it drives any decision.

The refuter's Lumibot claim (in-core lumibot/brokers/{alpaca.py, interactive_brokers.py, schwab.py, ...}) is a directory-listing assertion I did not open the upstream tree to confirm; the recommended action is a scheduled comparison precisely because that claim is unverified here.

agents-operations is compared only through wf1-layers.json selected[]/alternatives[]/overturn_when/next_action. I did not open catalogs/us-equities/agents-operations.md or agents-operations.json, and the T-runtimes sub-layer produces no evidence bearing on that layer, so the agents-operations side of this diff is a scope statement rather than a coverage measurement.

hftbacktest and pysystemtrade satisfy the literal 'absent' test (no repository-index.md row, no landscape candidate, no stack.json id) but both have architecture/trading.json source reviews; I listed them with that qualification rather than as missed discoveries.

Per-criterion sums (SUM=17 etc.) are arithmetic over the six 0-3 criteria as stored in the judges' scores; the judges themselves state they computed no averages or aggregates, so the sums are my presentation convenience and carry no authority the individual criteria do not.

Judge0's ranking contradicts its own rubric: it placed ML4T (criterion sum 15) at rank 1 above Vibe-Trading (sum 17, the highest raw total in the set, with 3/3 on four of six criteria). Whatever drove rank 1 is narrative preference not captured by the six scores, which means the six-criterion scores and the ranking are two different signals and should not be cited as if they corroborate each other.

Strong star anchoring in the shortlist: 8 of the 12 shortlisted repos have >8k stars and 6 have >20k, while the two repos the refuter had to re-introduce as better alternatives (skfolio 2,426 stars; purged-cross-validation 35 stars) are precisely the low-star ones — and the refuter says so explicitly about the second ('Its weakness is adoption (35 stars, 2 open issues)'). The mechanical merit pass has no star threshold in its stated drop reasons, so the anchoring entered at the shortlist/judging stage rather than the filter.

Auditable hole in the blind pipeline: 49 merged candidates minus 12 shortlisted minus 32 dropped leaves 5 with no recorded disposition — eslazarev/purged-cross-validation, stefan-jansen/alphalens-reloaded, HKUSTDial/DeepFund, HammerGPT/Hyper-Alpha-Arena and AlanJiang98/Awesome-LLM-Trading. Two of those five are directly on-topic for the sub-layer's named validation and factor-diagnostics areas, and purged-cross-validation had to be rediscovered by the refuter. Silent drops are a worse failure mode than a wrong drop reason.

The blind merit gate drops on GitHub's license metadata field alone ('license field is none/NOASSERTION, no recognised OSI SPDX id detected'), never on a LICENSE-file read. That single rule eliminated OpenBB, vectorbt, ElegantRL, live-trade-bench, alphagen, AlphaForge, QuantsPlaybook, financial-machine-learning and awesome-systematic-trading — including the two most method-specific formulaic-alpha-mining repos in the set. The catalog reaches the same unresolved state on vectorbt from the opposite direction ('subject to semantics/license fit'), so both passes are deferring the same cheap check.

The sub-layer boundary is doing more work than the evidence: the blind gate excluded skfolio, Riskfolio-Lib and PyPortfolioOpt from T-strategies as 'portfolio-optimization, not one of the sub-layer's named areas', then the refuter re-imported skfolio as a better alternative on the grounds that it ships CombinatorialPurgedCV and WalkForward — which IS one of the named areas. A definitional filter that the same pipeline later overrides is a bias vector, and it mirrors the catalog's own problem of bundling engines, broker SDK, validation, forecasting and RL under one engines-strategies layer_id.

Catalog-side structural bias: engines-strategies has exactly three disposition=selected candidates and all three are execution infrastructure (NautilusTrader 2.0.0rc5, LEAN 985ef30, alpaca-py 0.44.0). Every strategy-research repository in the layer sits at conditional, alternative or watch. So no blind-surfaced strategy source can ever be compared against a selected peer in this layer, and 'no promotion' is guaranteed by the layer's shape rather than earned by evidence. The layer's own verdict is 'corrected' with decision 'keep_but_compare' and saturation 'not_established', which is consistent with that reading.

Possible staleness bias in the catalog's China-benchmark reasoning: the qlib record is pinned to a v0.9.7 (2025-08-15) source read and its limitations extend the CSI300 caveat to RD-Agent by association. The blind refuter found a primary-source NASDAQ 100 evaluation with leakage-aware splits in RD-Agent's paper. The catalog's conclusion about qlib is independently confirmed; its inference about the adjacent repo was never re-checked.

Repository-string case and identity hygiene is a latent bias in any presence/absence diff of this kind: the wf1 record itself lists quantconnect/lean vs QuantConnect/Lean, tauricresearch/tradingagents vs TauricResearch/TradingAgents and lumiwealth/lumibot vs Lumiwealth/lumibot as known mismatches, and flags PyPortfolioOpt's org string (pyportfolio/pyportfolioopt) as carried forward unverified. I normalised case, but a rename or fork would still read as 'absent'.
limits: I executed no acceptance commands and derived no counts or exit codes by eye. Everything in blind_top, the merit metadata (stars, pushed_at, licenses, release dates), the code-search hit counts (61/56/68/13), the test-file counts (690/415/72/37/31) and the CI conclusions is quoted from /tmp/claude-1000/-home-seath-code-agent-lab/<PRIVATE_SESSION>/scratchpad/wf2-compact.json. I made no network call, ran no gh api, and re-verified none of the blind pass's upstream observations against GitHub, arXiv, ACM or PyPI. If the coordinator wants any of these treated as measured rather than reported, those commands need to be re-run and supplied.

Catalog presence/absence was determined by case-insensitive owner/repo and bare-slug grep over <PROJECTS_ROOT>/native-agent-stack-token-practice-review/catalogs, /manifests and <PROJECTS_ROOT>/native-agent-stack-landscape-finalization-20260921/catalogs. A repository recorded under a renamed owner, a fork, or by prose name only would be misreported as absent. The six repos I call absent (ML4T, RD-Agent, FinRL-Meta, FinRobot, tensortrade, je-suis-tm/quant-trading) returned zero hits on BOTH the owner/repo pattern and the bare slug, which is the strongest evidence this method produces but is not proof of absence from the catalog program as a whole.

I did not fully parse catalogs/us-equities/decision-index.json or coverage.json, which the repository-index.md header describes as the authoritative registered union. A row could in principle exist in one of those without surfacing in repository-index.md; my slug sweep covered them by text match only.

I did not read catalogs/us-equities/engines-strategies.md line by line. The line references (:38, :41-:47, :63, :65, :85, :93, :97) and the alternatives dispositions come from the wf1-layers.json record's alternatives[] array, not from my own read of that file. I did verify the engines-strategies.json entries for qlib, skfolio, finrl, tradingagents, pyportfolioopt and mlfinpy, and the repository-index.md rows, directly against source.

The blind artifact's own limits are inherited: modality limits note a gh api 404 during web discovery and that GitHub code search was used for the in-repo hit counts. Code-search counts are an indexing artifact, not a static analysis, and the refuter's own caveat (qlib implements walk-forward as RollingGen, 8 hits) shows the 0-columns measure vocabulary rather than capability. No finding here should rest on a hit count alone.

The refuter marked 3 of 10 claims refuted (ML4T's v3.1.0-artifacts totals, RD-Agent's no-US-evaluation clause, TradingAgents' de-leaking superlative). I did not independently re-check any refuter verdict against upstream, so the refutations are as unverified as the claims they overturn.

Five merged candidates appear in neither the shortlist nor the dropped list, so the blind pass's coverage of this sub-layer cannot be fully reconstructed from the artifact; the reason each was silently excluded is unrecoverable.

Evidence classes are not equivalent and I have not collapsed them: the catalog's skfolio claim is a locally executed bounded study with a receipt (blueprints/us-equities/research-evaluation/receipt.json), whereas every ML4T, Vibe-Trading, qlib and RD-Agent claim here is upstream CI status, code search or a published paper. No recommendation in this diff is backed by local execution against this project's data, and none of the scheduled comparisons has been run.

bias_observations: Name leakage into the supposedly catalog-free pass is explicit and documented in the blind artefact itself: the web modality's query list includes 'gh api orgs/alpacahq/repos --paginate' and 'nautilus trader data catalog parquet github' - the two vendors the project has already selected. alpaca-py, pymarketstore, alpaca-trade-api-python and nautilus_trader therefore cannot be treated as independent rediscoveries; nautilus_trader went on to place 3rd and 2nd in the two rankings.

Star anchoring in the shortlist gate. The 12-repo shortlist is close to star-ordered (OpenBB 73k, ClickHouse 50k, DuckDB 41.6k, Polars 39.8k, nautilus 29.2k, yfinance 25.3k, timescaledb 23.5k, Lean 21.7k, questdb 17.3k, arrow 17.1k, great_expectations 11.8k, FinanceDatabase 9.3k) - every eligible repo under ~9k stars was cut, including edgartools (2.7k), ArcticDB (2.5k), exchange_calendars (667) and databento-python (302). Both judges flagged this in their own limits, and the refuter had to re-introduce exactly those four as 'better alternatives found'. Star rank, not requirement coverage, drove which repos got judged.

The consequence is a shortlist with no dedicated tool for four of the sub-layer's own named requirements (exchange calendars, corporate actions, survivorship-bias-free universes, SEC/XBRL parsing), so judges were forced to attribute those capabilities to general infrastructure and to a backtest engine - which is precisely where the refuter found its three point-in-time refutations. Judge-0 states this plainly: 'ArcticDB in particular is a direct competitor to the storage rows here and its omission is material.'

License-rule asymmetry biases against exactly the artefacts this layer needs. Source-available/commercial terms were waived for high-star infrastructure after direct LICENSE reads (ArcticDB BUSL-1.1 and TimescaleDB dual-license both kept 'eligible'), while small reference/dataset repos were dropped mechanically for a missing LICENSE file (teddykoker/survivorship-free-spy, leogregianin/stock-exchange-holidays). A survivorship-bias-free dataset repo is dropped on a formality while a BUSL database is kept.

Awesome-list echo is present but mild: 'awesome quant github curated list market data' was a discovery query and wilsonfreitas/awesome-quant was itself carried as a candidate row (dropped only for a missing LICENSE, not for being a list). Several shortlisted repos are awesome-quant staples, so some apparent multi-modality convergence may be one list observed twice.

Catalog-side discovery frame is also star-derived: every relevant repository-index.md row is provenance-labelled 'Starred' or 'Beyond stars' (e.g. :185, :259, :270, :364, :366), i.e. rows enter through the maintainer's star graph. That is consistent with the three in-scope, actively maintained repos that have no row anywhere (timescaledb, FinanceDatabase, ibind) and with the layer having QuestDB and ClickHouse but not TimescaleDB.

Both passes are documentary. The blind side executed no code and ran no benchmark (stated in both judges' limits); the catalog side records dispositions against 'checked release' strings. Neither side has measured evidence for any storage or throughput claim in this layer, so agreement between them is not corroboration.

Cross-layer signal, flagged for T-engines rather than claimed here: repository-index.md:289 records nautechsystems/nautilus_trader as 'engines-strategies: alternative' while AGENTS.md names NautilusTrader 2.0.0rc5 as the selected destination. The index label and the project's stated selection do not agree.
limits: No acceptance command was run and no count or exit code was derived by eye. All GitHub metadata quoted (stars, pushed_at, licenses, releases, archived flags, workflow-run counts) comes from the blind pass's own artefact dated 2026-09-21; I did not re-query GitHub and cannot independently confirm any of it. If the coordinator wants it verified, the checks are gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>, .../releases/latest and .../actions/workflows for the named repos.

Presence/absence was established by case-insensitive substring grep (grep -ril) over *.md and *.json in <PROJECTS_ROOT>/native-agent-stack-token-practice-review and <PROJECTS_ROOT>/native-agent-stack-landscape-finalization-20260921, plus manifests/stack.json. A component recorded under a different spelling, a bare URL variant or a non-md/json file would be missed, and the same method can produce false presence for short names. The dbn case shows the method working in both directions: absent from repository-index.md, present in convergence-program/trading.md:21.
Catalog files were read from the working tree at the paths given in the task, not from a checked-out main. Both repos may have uncommitted state; I did not diff against origin/main.

Judge score sums were computed in code by adding the six criterion fields from wf2-compact.json; I did not re-derive or re-review any individual score, and where a judge omitted a repo from its top-5 I used its scores[] entry instead of a stated rank.

catalogs/us-equities/data-research.json - the machine record that repository-index.md links its dispositions to - was not opened. Dispositions cited here come from wf1-layers.json, the data-research.md tables (lines ~50-145) and repository-index.md rows. wf1 itself records that disposition labels diverge between the Sept-19 markdown and the current landscape JSON for at least seven components in this layer (DVC, Pandera, sec-edgar-downloader, OpenBB, Polars, lakeFS, yfinance), so 'the catalog disposition' is not single-valued for those.

The blind pass's merit modality ran no independent discovery ('this sub-task was purely mechanical gh api metadata collection on a pre-supplied candidate list'), so the 43-repo candidate pool reflects one earlier discovery pass, not repeated independent sampling. Absence from that pool is weak evidence of absence from the field.

Refuter findings were read from the artefact, not re-verified against upstream. Two are worth re-checking before acting: the NautilusTrader point-in-time refutation was done against develop-branch docs while the project targets 2.0.0rc5, and the DuckDB workflow-run counts (coverity total_count=0, cifuzz 9 lifetime runs) are time-sensitive Actions API results.

bias_observations: NAME LEAKAGE INTO THE 'BLIND' PASS IS DIRECT AND MEASURABLE. Of the 22 recorded web queries, at least 7 name specific repositories or vendors rather than describing a capability: 'alternatives to pyfolio quantstats tearsheet', 'cvxportfolio convex optimization portfolio github', 'empyrical alphalens pyfolio reloaded maintained fork github', 'OpenBB Qlib FinRL portfolio risk github', 'PyPortfolioOpt mlfinlab backtrader vectorbt zipline reloaded github', 'QuantLib Microsoft Qlib AI4Finance FinRL github organization' and - the clearest catalog leak - 'alpaca markets github open source trading algorithms'. Alpaca is a catalog-selected component; seeding its name in a catalog-free pass means the blind/catalog agreement on alpaca-py is not independent evidence.

THE GITHUB MODALITY SEEDS THE SAME NAMES. Its query list includes `q='pyfolio OR quantstats stars:>50'`, `q='pyfolio stars:>10'` and direct org enumerations `gh api orgs/cvxgrp/repos`, `orgs/skfolio/repos`, `orgs/quantopian/repos`. cvxgrp, skfolio and quantopian are all existing catalog rows, so three of the modality's org-level sweeps were aimed at already-catalogued organisations.

STAR ANCHORING IS STRUCTURAL, NOT INCIDENTAL. The merit step's shortlist rule is literally a 12-repository cap applied to a star ranking ('rank #N of 31 passers by star count'), and every dropped-but-passing row records its star rank as the cut reason. The consequence is measurable in the judges' own scores: four of the twelve shortlist slots went to repos BOTH judges scored capability_fit=1 (OpenBB 73k stars, FinRL 16k, QuantLib 7.6k, FinancePy 3.1k), while maintained, currently-released, on-topic small repos were cut unjudged - tschm/pyhrp (55 stars, v2.3.3 2026-06-25), fortitudo-tech/entropy-pooling (41, v1.0.9), ArturSepp/OptimalPortfolios (95, v7.6.0 2026-09-14), convexfi/riskparity.py (325), fortitudo-tech/fortitudo.tech (310, v1.2.5), dcelisgarza/PortfolioOptimisers.jl (25, v0.31.1). Star count decided the judged set; capability did not.

THE BLIND PASS ADDED ALMOST NOTHING THE CATALOG LACKS. All three of the refuter's better_alternatives_found - cvxgrp/cvxportfolio, pmorissette/ffn, pmorissette/bt - are already catalog rows (repository-index.md:134, :343, :342 and engines-strategies.md:66, :67, :46). The only genuinely new shortlisted/ranked repos are pysystemtrade, QuantLib and FinancePy, and both judges scored the latter two capability_fit=1. That is a convergence result, but it is weakened as independent corroboration by the name leakage above.

AWESOME-LIST ECHO IS USED AS CORROBORATION. skfolio's merge record justifies it partly with 'cross-validated in independent awesome-quant listing', and one of the web queries is 'awesome quant github curated list portfolio risk'. Presence on a curated list is circulation, not evidence; it should not count as a second modality confirming the first.

JUDGE LENSES CANNOT REACH THE CATALOG'S ACTUAL DECISION CRITERION. Judge-1's own limits state 'Per the blindness rule, no file under <PROJECTS_ROOT> was opened ... The consequence is that fit to any already-chosen execution engine, adapter or data layer is not assessed here - capability_fit measures only coverage of the five stated sub-layer functions.' The engines-strategies overturn_when is defined in terms of Nautilus cash/order semantics, SPY/LEAN parity and broker reconciliation. No blind score in this sub-layer can therefore satisfy or overturn the catalog's criterion, and none should be read as doing so.

FAVOURABLE-EXCLUSIVITY FRAMING IN THE JUDGE OUTPUT. Of five Judge-1 sota_claims, three were about skfolio and the refuter had to narrow two of them (the CI-exclusivity claim was refuted outright by PyPortfolioOpt's broader matrix; the cost-modelling claim survived only after removing transaction costs and previous-weight turnover from the exclusivity, which PyPortfolioOpt also ships). The refuter also caught an origination claim crediting EVaR to Riskfolio-Lib's maintainer when it is Ahmadi-Javid (JOTA 2012). The refute stage is doing real work; the judge stage on its own over-claims exclusivity for its top pick.
limits: I ran no acceptance commands and executed no code against any candidate repository. Every GitHub fact cited here - stars, pushed_at, licence text, workflow conclusions, commit counts, release dates - is the blind pass's own 2026-09-21/22 snapshot as recorded in wf2-compact.json, re-read but NOT independently re-verified by me. If any of those snapshots is wrong, the disagreements built on it are wrong in the same direction.

The per-layer JSON files that repository-index.md links (engines-strategies.json) were not read. Catalog dispositions cited come from <PROJECTS_ROOT>/native-agent-stack-token-practice-review/catalogs/us-equities/repository-index.md rows, the engines-strategies.md tables, <PROJECTS_ROOT>/native-agent-stack-landscape-finalization-20260921/catalogs/landscape/us-equities.json candidates and the wf1-layers.json engines-strategies record. A disposition stated only in engines-strategies.json could differ.

The absence check was a case-insensitive substring grep for owner/repo slug and bare repo name across repository-index.md, star-audit.md, all catalogs/us-equities/*.md, both landscape JSONs and manifests/stack.json. A repo recorded under a superseded owner string would read as absent. I specifically guarded the most important case: 'pysystemtrade' AND 'robcarver' both return zero hits across all of those sources, so that absence is solid. Short names produced substring noise that I re-checked precisely (bashtage/arch, ml4t/backtest, lakshmiDRIP/DROP, DaniyalMlk/slippage - the latter three confirmed absent).

Version mismatch not resolved: catalogs/us-equities/engines-strategies.md records alphalens-reloaded at 0.4.6 while the blind merit row reports latest GitHub release 0.4.5 (2025-07-23). This may be a PyPI-versus-GitHub-tag difference rather than an error; I did not query either index to settle it.

Numerical correctness was assessed for nothing. Both judges say so explicitly, and I add nothing: no optimizer output, covariance estimator, risk-measure definition or tearsheet statistic was compared against a reference by the blind pass or by me. 'evidence' scores measure whether tests exist and run, not whether the maths is right.
No judge or modality examined installability on this machine's Python 3.12+/WSL2 environment. Claims about lifecycle_portability are readings of classifiers, requires-python bounds and CI matrices.

Judge score sums reported here were computed with jq over the artifact's per-criterion integers, not read off by eye. But the criteria weights are equal by assumption - the artifact provides no weighting - so a sum is a convenience, not a ranking the judges themselves asserted; where sums and stated rankings diverge (e.g. Judge-1 ranks pysystemtrade #2 at sum 14 while FinancePy also sums to 14), I used the judges' explicit ranking arrays.

The blind sub-layer's discovery was confined to two modalities (web, github) on a single day and its own judges note that 90-day activity counters can misread projects that batch work or develop on non-default branches - skfolio, vectorbt and PyPortfolioOpt all showed feature-branch traffic a default-branch count would miss. Maintenance-based findings inherit that error bar.

I did not read docs/full-stack-convergence.md or docs/foundation-closure-20260921.md, so if either already records a dated disposition for pysystemtrade, QuantLib, FinancePy, fortitudo-tech or pyhrp, my 'absent from catalog' findings for those would need to be downgraded to 'absent from the four sources I was given'.

bias_observations: Destination-name anchoring in a supposedly catalog-free pass: the blind merit step ranked nautechsystems/nautilus_trader FIRST in the shortlist for an Alpaca sub-layer on the basis of an open RFC issue, and judge1 called this out in its own limits — 'a code search for alpaca across that repository returns zero files. Generic engineering excellence was allowed to substitute for sub-layer capability. This is precisely the synthesis bias the review was asked to detect.' Nautilus is the catalog's selected destination, so its presence at the top of a catalog-free shortlist is the single strongest leakage signal in this diff. Both judges then corrected it to capability_fit 0 and 1 respectively, so the leakage was caught at the judging stage, not the discovery stage.

Star-count anchoring is structural, not incidental, in the blind pass: the merit step's own dropped[] entries state that alpaca-java, alpacahq/agentic, alpacadecimal, d-e-s-o/apcacli, dm13450/AlpacaMarkets.jl and Magica-Chen/GaussWorldTrader 'passed all mechanical rules but cut by the 12-repo shortlist cap, ranked by star count'. That removed the official Java SDK (3 stars, actively released) while retaining lower-merit entries with more stars, and both judges were then explicitly constrained to the truncated shortlist.

Awesome-list echo chamber, self-reported by the blind pass: the org modality's limits record that a broad GitHub search 'surfaced mostly irrelevant huge awesome-lists (public-apis, ccxt, awesome-rust) before relevant hits appeared lower in relevance'. TauricResearch/TradingAgents (107,976 stars) entered the candidate set only because it was 'cited only alongside Alpaca MCP coverage in a curated list', and was then dropped for having no Alpaca integration of its own — a pure list-adjacency artefact.

Asymmetric relevance bar in the blind pass: freqtrade, vnpy, jesse, hummingbot, hikyuu, OctoBot, ccxt, FinRL, ai-hedge-fund and backtesting.py were all dropped for 'no stated Alpaca adapter/integration in candidate evidence', while nautilus_trader was admitted and top-ranked on an unmerged RFC issue. The same standard applied symmetrically would have dropped Nautilus at the merit stage.

Blind merit metadata is systematically corrupted in a way that would bias any mechanical re-ranking: EVERY merit row reports open_issues=0 while the API reports 87 (alpaca-py), 129 (nautilus_trader), 90 (lumibot), 57 (alpaca-backtrader-api), 43 (go), 27 (csharp), 23 (mcp-server), 19 (apca); has_tests='no' is wrong for alpaca-trade-api-go, alpaca-trade-api-csharp and d-e-s-o/apca, while has_tests='yes' for alpaca-backtrader-api means one file. Both judges independently flagged this and rebuilt scores from primary sources.

pushed_at as a freshness proxy actively admits abandoned repositories: alpaca-backtrader-api passed the blind 12-month freshness rule on pushed_at 2026-06-23 while its default branch has been frozen since 2022-01-02, the 2026 activity being pyup and dependabot branches. Judge1 states the correct field is default-branch commit date. Any catalog or blind filter keyed on pushed_at inherits this bias.

Catalog-side discovery-modality bias: catalogs/us-equities/star-audit.md contains no alpacahq rows at all, and the blind-absent set (AlpacaTradingAgent, apca, QuantDinger, StrateQueue, GaussWorldTrader, AlpacaMarkets.jl) is likewise absent from the catalog's star-derived layer. The catalog's Alpaca coverage comes almost entirely from one deliberate org enumeration (architecture/alpaca-organization.json, 94 repositories, checked 2026-09-19), whose own scope line says 'metadata enumeration is not source review or runtime acceptance'. So catalog breadth here is a product of targeting, and anything outside the alpacahq org that is not publicly starred is structurally invisible to it — which is exactly where the four genuinely-new blind finds sit.

No reverse leakage detected: nothing in the blind judge or refuter output cites a catalog path, manifest, pin or task record, and both judges state their lens prose was scored 'blind from public GitHub/web evidence... no project catalog, manifest or task record was opened'. The Alpaca-specific vocabulary in the blind output (paper/live parity, corporate actions, --adjustment) is traceable to alpacahq/alpaca-skills' own reference.md rather than to catalog text.

Convergent-agreement risk to guard against: on nautilus_trader the catalog (README.md:95, engines-strategies.md:50) and both blind judges reach the same conclusion. That agreement is genuine but is NOT independent confirmation of the destination choice — it is two passes reading the same upstream adapter list. The catalog's own policy of not promoting by agreement applies here in reverse: agreement about an absence is still only documentary.
limits: Nothing in this diff was executed or verified against GitHub by me. Every upstream fact (star counts, pushed_at, licence fields, CI matrices, RFC/PR states, file listings, issue counts) is as-reported by the blind pass's judges and refuter, dated 2026-09-21. Both judges state explicitly that no repository was cloned, built, installed or run and that all scores are documentary; judge2 adds 'no claim here rests on observed runtime behaviour, measured latency, actual fill realism, or reproduced backtest output'. I ran no acceptance command and made no network call.

Catalog membership was determined by case-normalised owner/repo regex over catalogs/us-equities/repository-index.md, star-audit.md, all catalogs/us-equities/*.md, manifests/stack.json, and the landscape foundation.json and us-equities.json, then cross-checked against decision-index.json's 513 records. A repository recorded only under an alias, or in a table row carrying no GitHub URL, would be missed — the wf1 layer record itself notes engines-strategies.md carries URLs on only 12 lines (15 unique repos), and that catalog-ID-only rows such as alpaca-backtrader-legacy exist. My first membership pass had a string-normalisation defect that truncated repository names; the reported results come from the corrected pass.

The three-source absence test specified in the task (no repository-index.md row, no landscape candidate, no stack.json id) produces false positives against this catalog. alpaca-trade-api-js/go/csharp and alpaca-mcp-server pass that test yet carry dispositions in catalogs/us-equities/architecture/alpaca.json via decision-index.json; alpaca-skills and alpacahq/cli pass it yet carry dated pinned rows in paper-practice-20260921.md. I report those separately from the genuinely-absent set, but a reader applying the literal test would overstate the gap.

The Lumibot licence question is unresolved on BOTH sides and I could not close it: the catalog's conflict is between the v4.5.91 tag's LICENSE and that tag's setup.py (engines-strategies.md:52), whereas the refuter verified GPL-3.0 from the default branch (dev). No evidence in either input speaks to the tagged release.

I read the catalog markdown plus decision-index.json, architecture/alpaca.json and architecture/alpaca-organization.json; I did not open the underlying engines-strategies.json, data-research.json, star-audit.json or coverage.json records that those files point at. Disposition strings quoted here come from the markdown tables and the decision index, so a divergence inside the unread JSON records would not be visible to me.

Blind coverage of the sub-layer is incomplete by the blind pass's own account. The merged set holds 68 candidates touching 38 alpacahq repositories; the catalog's org record holds 94. I verified the blind pass touched ZERO alpacahq repositories the catalog org record lacks, so no org-level discovery claim can be made in the blind pass's favour. The org modality also reports 93 enumerated rows against 94 expected without resolving the discrepancy, and the web modality states it 'did not exhaustively search gh code/gh search repos for every possible third-party Alpaca adapter', relying on web-surfaced roundups — so the four genuinely-new third-party finds are a floor, not a complete set.

No repository in this sub-layer publishes a point-in-time-correctness or look-ahead audit of its own Alpaca integration (judge2's stated limit), and survivorship/delisted-universe handling is unestablished across the entire sub-layer with zero 'survivorship' hits in lumibot or the Alpaca backtest skill. The catalog independently requires exactly this at catalogs/us-equities/data-research.md:101 ('Keep delisted securities and historical membership'), so the gap is a real open requirement on both sides and not resolvable from this diff.

exchange_calendars could not be assessed from either side: it is data-research disposition=selected but has no manifests/stack.json entry and no catalogs/landscape/upstream-snapshot.json component (per the wf1 record, which I did not independently re-verify), and it is out of scope for the Alpaca sub-layer so the blind pass says nothing about it. Its licence remains 'not recorded in any read source'.

The scoring sums in blind_top are my arithmetic over the six per-criterion judge scores (capability_fit, evidence, maintenance_provenance, license_deployment_fit, lifecycle_portability, quality_cost; max 18). The judges published per-criterion scores and an ordered ranking but no totals, and their published rankings are not strictly monotonic in these sums — e.g. judge1 ranks alpaca-py (16) above alpaca-mcp-server (17) and alpaca-trade-api-js (17). Treat the sums as a reading aid, not as the judges' own ordering.

bias_observations: Blind pass, self-reported and severe: the merit agent's own limits[] carries a 'CRITICAL BIAS FINDING' that naive GitHub sort=stars in this environment returns heavily star-farmed repositories interleaved with legitimate ones, with five verified examples exceeding canonical org repos - affaan-m/ECC at 264,775, NousResearch/hermes-agent at 247,796, farion1231/cc-switch at 133,982, DietrichGebert/ponytail at 143,760 (a joke-description repo), nextlevelbuilder/ui-ux-pro-max-skill at 129,606, all above openai/codex (125,778) and google-gemini/gemini-cli (107,123). The agent mitigated this by switching to direct gh api repos/<owner>/<repo> lookups, but the star numbers that then drove the shortlist cap are the same class of number.

Blind pass, structural: 32 of 40 candidates passed the four mechanical filters against a 12-slot cap, and the tie-break used was stars-descending - the agent flagged this itself as a choice that should be reviewed. Both judges independently named it as the dominant bias in their own limits[]. The excluded set is systematically the purpose-built infrastructure the sub-layer is about: e2b-dev/E2B (13,905), dagger/container-use (4,046), block/agent-task-queue (68), nekocode/agent-worktree (278), SWE-agent/SWE-agent (20,384), microsoft/agent-framework (13,706), anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python (8,144). Every small purpose-built tool lost to every large general platform by construction.

Blind pass: the top-ranked entry by stars, deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness (232,398 stars, 27,899 forks at ~5.5 weeks of age, 36 contributors, 994 watchers), could not be corroborated from any independent source. The research judge responded correctly by excluding stars and forks from every criterion for all twelve, but the shortlist that produced those twelve was still built on the same numbers.

Blind pass, internal inconsistency: the engineering judge ranked openai/codex #1 with score sum 14 while cline, goose and OpenHands each summed to 15 under its own six criteria. The ranking is therefore not a function of the published scores, and the repo it elevated is the largest-vendor incumbent - consistent with name anchoring, though the judge's notes give a substantive rationale (deepest verified isolation+SDK surface). Worth noting because this sub-layer's #1 is the catalog's Default.

Blind pass, mechanical filter as a hidden selection effect: the 'recognised OSI licence' rule dropped anthropics/claude-code, anthropics/skills, daytonaio/daytona (all licence-404) plus charmbracelet/crush, mastra-ai/mastra, vercel/ai and manaflow-ai/cmux (licence.key='other'). That rule structurally cannot rank proprietary or non-SPDX-mappable tools, i.e. it can never evaluate the catalog's primary native client. The merit agent flagged that a manual LICENSE text read was out of scope.

Catalog, discovery anchored to the operator's own stars: catalogs/convergence-practice/public-starred.json is a 342-repository personal star snapshot and the repository-index/star-audit disposition universe is built on it (337 public stars plus 116 beyond). Everything the blind pass found absent - gemini-cli, opencode, crewAI, aider, SWE-agent, kilocode, continue, qwen-code, pydantic-ai, mastra, crush, trae-agent - is absent in exactly the way a personal-star-derived universe is absent. This is a reach limitation, not an error, but it should be stated wherever the catalog's coverage counts are cited.

Catalog, awesome-list echo chamber with an explicit accounting: architecture/coverage-accounting.json records 12 awesome-list sources yielding 7,028 extracted GitHub identities of which 6,939 are discovery_only_unassessed and only 4 reached selected_source_review. microsoft/autogen and paul-gauthier/aider exist in the catalog ONLY as category keys inside the e2b-dev/awesome-ai-agents README dump. The catalog is honest about this (the counts are published), but 'present in the index' and 'assessed' are very different states for the F-agents sub-layer, and the blanket rationale at convergence-practice/source-review.md:21 ('duplicate an existing role or have no demonstrated gap') was applied to that whole tail at once.

Blindness held on the north-star side: across the whole F-agents record there are zero occurrences of 'nautilus', 'IBKR' or 'agent-lab', and one incidental 'alpaca'. 'US equities' and 'backtest' appear only inside the research judge's own declared lens, which is by design. No catalog-selected repository name (worktrunk, mcporter, sandbox-runtime, agentskills, typesafe) leaked into the blind output; affaan-m/ECC appears once and demonstrably arrived via GitHub star-sorted search, not via catalog knowledge. The blind/catalog separation for this sub-layer can be treated as intact.
limits: I ran no acceptance command, no gh api call and no network lookup. Every star count, push date, licence string, release tag and benchmark figure in this report is quoted from the blind artifact at /tmp/claude-1000/-home-seath-code-agent-lab/<PRIVATE_SESSION>/scratchpad/wf2-compact.json or from catalog files on disk. None of it was re-verified against GitHub by me. If a figure is load-bearing for an action, ask the coordinator to re-run the lookup.

Presence/absence was determined by case-insensitive owner/repo slug substring matching over 1,897 text files (.md/.json/.jsonl/.toml/.yaml/.yml) in <PROJECTS_ROOT>/native-agent-stack-token-practice-review and <PROJECTS_ROOT>/native-agent-stack-landscape-finalization-20260921. I additionally checked the four known historical aliases (sst/opencode, block/goose, All-Hands-AI, paul-gauthier/aider) - all zero except paul-gauthier/aider in the awesome-list dump - but a repository recorded under some OTHER unlisted former name would read as absent. The absence claims are as strong as that alias list.

repository-index.md itself states that decision-index.json is now the authoritative union and the visible table is a frozen 2026-09-19 snapshot. I matched against the sources the task named (repository-index.md, star-audit, the us-equities layer tables, landscape foundation.json/us-equities.json, stack.json) plus a whole-repo sweep, but I did not parse decision-index.json as a structured index, so an entry present only there would be caught by the sweep only if the slug appears literally.

Both blind judges state that nothing was executed, cloned, installed or built; every score is documentary (GitHub API metadata, git trees, README/docs, release assets, published advisories). Capability_fit therefore reflects code-present capability, not demonstrated behaviour, and quality_cost is the weakest column throughout - no latency, token or dollar figure was measured for any candidate.

The blind merit metadata is known to contain at least two errors that both judges caught independently (langchain-ai/langgraph has_tests='no' is wrong - 248 test paths exist; deepseek-harness open_issues=0 means the tracker is disabled, which inverts the field's meaning). The merit agent itself warns its root-only contents listing can mis-mark nested monorepo tests, naming anomalyco/opencode. Other rows in the same table may carry uncorrected errors; the has_tests/has_ci columns in particular should not be relied on.

Benchmark evidence is secondary throughout. The judge could not read the primary tbench.ai leaderboard (JavaScript-rendered, empty table body) and used an aggregator; the refuter's Terminal-Bench 2.1 figures come from a third-party leaderboard page. The mini-SWE-agent 76.2% figure that drives one add-candidate-row recommendation has not been confirmed against the primary leaderboard by either pass or by me.

The blind shortlist was capped at 12 of 32 mechanically-passing candidates, and both judges scored only those 12. For the 28 dropped candidates I have merit metadata and a drop reason but no scores, so 'the judges rated it' in blind_found_absent_from_catalog is only available for the shortlisted subset; for crewAI, herdr and autogen I have scores, for the refuter's alternatives I have only its discovery reasoning.

I read the catalog layer records through the wf1-layers.json extraction plus direct reads of repository-index.md, star-audit.json, agents-operations.json, coverage-accounting.json, public-starred.json and convergence-practice/source-review.md. I did NOT open foundation.json line-by-line to re-verify the line numbers (:17, :30, :37, :43, :50, :56) that the wf1 record cites; those citations are carried through from that record. The wf1 record's own corrections[] indicate its selected[]/alternatives[] arrays were partly wrong before correction, so the corrected membership I used for workers and isolation is the corrected set, not the raw extraction.

bias_observations: STAR ANCHORING IN THE BLIND PASS, SELF-DECLARED: merit.limits states that the mechanical rules (not archived, pushed<=12mo or release<=18mo, OSI licence, relevance) left 33 of 40 candidates passing, and that 'to cut to the requested cap without a subjective merit call, a second purely mechanical tiebreak (GitHub star count) was applied to select the top 12 by stars'. Every downstream judge score and ranking in this sub-layer is therefore conditioned on a star ranking. The three most-starred candidates (vLLM 92370, RAGFlow 91116, PaddleOCR 89960) entered the shortlist on stars and finished at the bottom of both judges' score tables (eng 13/11/13, res 14/11/16) - direct evidence the star cut selected against merit.

THE STAR CUT DELETED AN ENTIRE NAMED SLOT: the sub-layer definition opens with 'code navigation and retrieval (LSP/symbol tools, structural search, code RAG)', yet none of the twelve shortlisted repositories is a code-navigation or structural-search tool - the shortlist is entirely document ingestion, vector stores and agent memory. The refuter identified this independently as a coverage gap rather than a ranking error. Serena, ast-grep, tree-sitter, Semgrep, Zoekt, SeaGOAT, probe, claude-context and multilspy were all discovered and all eliminated before judging.

MECHANICAL LICENCE FILTER BIASED AGAINST THE CATALOG'S OWN CHOICES: the blind rule dropped Serena, pgvector, Weaviate and Sourcebot on GitHub license.spdx_id=NOASSERTION. Serena is the catalog's code-navigation and foundation-memory default; pgvector is a catalog conditional. merit.limits itself concedes 'this is GitHub's own license-detector output, not a legal finding'. The same rule would silently exclude Context Mode (Elastic-2.0, upstream NOASSERTION) and jCodeMunch (Dual-Use License 1.1) if they had been discovered - so any blind/catalog coverage diff built this way systematically under-reports overlap on non-OSI tooling.

NO TRADING-DOMAIN NAME LEAKAGE DETECTED IN THIS SUB-LAYER: none of the 40 merged candidates is an Alpaca, IBKR or Nautilus component, and judge 1 states explicitly that 'none of the twelve shortlisted repositories is a trading-domain tool' and that US-equities correctness had to be operationalised indirectly via four proxy properties. That is a clean blindness result, but it also means every 'US-equities fit' score in this sub-layer is inferential rather than measured against any equities task.

THE JUDGES CONTRADICT EACH OTHER AND THE REFUTER CAUGHT IT: the engineering judge asserted FAISS was 'the only shortlisted vector component with a dedicated peer-reviewed library paper' while the research judge asserted Milvus has the strongest peer-reviewed provenance (ACM SIGMOD 2021). Both cannot hold; the refuter resolved it against FAISS (arXiv:2401.08281 lists no venue; the repo's own citation block records journal={arXiv preprint}). Two independent judges converging on a top-5 is therefore not evidence of correctness in this sub-layer - agreement and error coexisted.

VENDOR AND COMPARISON-CONTENT SOURCES ARE DOING REAL WORK ON BOTH SIDES: the refuter had to reject AIMultiple (a commercial comparison-content site) as the basis for the Milvus benchmark claim, and its own strongest LanceDB argument rests on docs.lancedb.com plus that same AIMultiple table. Two of the four better_alternatives_found evidence URLs are particula.tech blog posts. The blind lane's non-primary evidence is not uniformly stronger than the catalog's source_review cards.

CATALOG-SIDE DISCOVERY IS ALSO STAR-SHAPED: repository-index.md's Discovery column has exactly two values, 'Starred' and 'Beyond stars', and a separate star-audit.md/star-audit.json pair drives dispositions. Six of the repos in this diff carry the review depth 'prior_evidence_link · already_covered' (mem0, cognee, OpenViking, supermemory, ragflow, serena) - a label that closes review by pointing at an earlier link rather than at a measured comparison. The mem0 case shows this concretely: new dated non-vendor benchmark evidence (LongMemEval reversal) exists for a repo the catalog marked as already covered.

THE CATALOG'S SMALL-REPO SELECTIONS ARE INVISIBLE TO GITHUB-ONLY DISCOVERY, WHICH FLATTERS BOTH SIDES: merit.limits records that no web-search modality was needed because 'all 39 candidates in the computed-task list already carried a GitHub repository_url', so the blind candidate set is exactly what its seed list contained. Consequently ai-memory (the SOLE durable-memory selection), QMD, Context Hub, jCodeMunch, codebase-memory-mcp, SocratiCode, Context Mode and RTK were never tested by the blind pass at all. The absence of blind criticism of these components is a discovery artifact, not a clean bill of health.

AGPL IS APPLIED INCONSISTENTLY ACROSS THE TWO PASSES AND WITHIN THE BLIND PASS: the refuter treats AGPL-3.0 as a genuine blocker for MinerU in a closed proprietary stack, while the engineering judge scored cognee (AGPL-3.0) 3/3 on license_deployment_fit, and the catalog itself selects SocratiCode (AGPL-3.0-only) at semantic-rag and foundation-memory. No single licence policy is being applied.
limits: I ran no acceptance commands and executed nothing. All GitHub metadata (stars, pushed_at, licence, latest_release, archived) is quoted from merit.rows inside wf2-compact.json as the blind pass recorded it on 2026-09-21/22; I did not re-fetch any of it. The blind pass's own limits note that pushed_at values cluster within hours of the system date and were not cross-checked against a second source.

The refute.verdicts objects have keys [claim, reason, refuted, repository_url, source] - `refuted` is a boolean with no confidence score and there is no per-criterion numeric verdict. My 'REFUTED'/'SURVIVOR' labels are that boolean plus the free-text reason, nothing more.

Absence claims in blind_found_absent_from_catalog rest on case-insensitive regex sweeps over *.md and *.json in <PROJECTS_ROOT>/native-agent-stack-token-practice-review and <PROJECTS_ROOT>/native-agent-stack-landscape-finalization-20260921. A repository referenced only under a different name, only as a bare URL with different casing, or only in a non-md/json file would be missed. I confirmed the two near-misses ('chroma' and 'fastembed') are transitive dependency mentions inside candidates.json/public-starred.json, not candidate rows.

I read catalogs/us-equities/foundation-memory.json, catalogs/us-equities/repository-index.md and catalogs/us-equities/star-audit.json as original source. The other per-layer tables (agents-operations.md, data-research.md, etc.) and catalogs/landscape/foundation.json + us-equities.json were only grep-swept, not read; layer-level dispositions for code-navigation, document-retrieval, semantic-rag and durable-memory come from wf1-layers.json, which is itself an extracted-and-corrected record rather than the catalog file. Any disposition I attribute to those four layers should be re-checked against catalogs/landscape/foundation.json lines 63-126 before it is acted on.

The catalog-selected repositories list also comes from wf1-layers.json selected[]. wf1 flags that several of those records needed correction (canonical casing for SocratiCode/OpenViking/LightRAG; stack.json repository fields being release-tag URLs rather than bare repo URLs; foundation-memory.md line 9 saying ai-memory v2.3.1 while stack.json says 2.3.2). I used the corrected values but did not independently verify stack.json line numbers.

No comparison, benchmark or retrieval run was performed by me or by the blind pass - the blind judges state every score is documentary and that nothing was installed, executed or benchmarked. Every recommended_catalog_action is therefore a scheduling or record-hygiene action; none of them is supported by measured evidence and none should be read as authorising a default change.

Judge score sums are my arithmetic over the six per-criterion integers in judges[].scores[]; the judges themselves published only rankings, not sums, and did not state that the six criteria are equally weighted. Treat the sums as a presentation aid, not as the judges' own ordering - note that judge 1's ranking (FAISS, Qdrant, Docling) does not follow from its own scores, which tie all three at 18.

I could not attribute merit rows to repositories by name for four low-relevance entries (the 24735-star 'Agent Memory That Learns' row, the 28688-star 'Persistent memory for AI coding agents' row, the 7293-star AGPL 'Memory library for building stateful agents' row, and the 23386-star RAG-Anything row) because merit.rows was matched to the merged[] list by description and star count. None of these four is load-bearing for any finding above, but if the catalog wants a complete absent-from-catalog list rather than the shortlisted/ranked set the task asked for, those four need explicit owner/repo resolution first.

Coverage of blind_found_absent_from_catalog is scoped as the task specified - shortlisted or ranked repositories only. Weaviate, Chroma, Unstructured, Semgrep, tree-sitter, sourcebot-dev/sourcebot, kantord/SeaGOAT, qdrant/fastembed, probelabs/probe, plastic-labs/honcho, oraios/multilspy and wrale/mcp-server-tree-sitter were all surfaced by blind discovery and all have zero rows in either catalog repo, but were cut before ranking (by the star tiebreak, the NOASSERTION licence rule, or the archived rule) so I did not give them individual entries.

bias_observations: Star-count anchoring decided which repositories were judged at all. The 12-entry shortlist is exactly the top 12 of the 46 merit rows by star count (183,000 / 146,826 / 115,786 / 96,478 / 95,607 / 91,116 / 73,422 / 52,270 / 43,006 / 39,805 / 38,189 / 37,460), with no capability or fit criterion applied at the cut. The merit row for microsoft/playwright-mcp says so explicitly: 'not in top-12 shortlist by star count but passes all mechanical filter rules'. It was excluded at 37,453 stars while khoj-ai/khoj entered at 37,460 — a 7-star margin — and both judges then rated khoj the weakest candidate in the set (maintenance_provenance 1, last push 2026-08-02, release 2.0.0-beta.28 from 2026-03-26). A single arbitrary star boundary put a dead repo in front of the judges and kept a live Microsoft-maintained one out.

The mechanical NOASSERTION licence rule removed the entire dedicated-eval category before judging. openai/evals (19,489 stars), Arize-ai/phoenix (11,567) and langfuse/langfuse (34,912) were all dropped because `gh api repos/<repo>/license` returned spdx_id=NOASSERTION / name=Other — a GitHub classification failure that the merit limits correctly label 'a detection-tool limitation, not a claim the projects are unlicensed', and that the catalog contradicts directly (Elastic-2.0 for Phoenix, MIT-core-plus-ee for langfuse). This is the mechanism behind the refuter's finding that 'neither judge ranked a single dedicated eval framework — both rankings are browser automation, prompt optimisation and retrieval only', in a sub-layer whose own definition names 'quality/evaluation frameworks (LLM eval)' as one of its three thirds.

Vendor-blog echo chamber in the discovery and evidence layer. Judge 1's browser-use SOTA claim rested on brightdata.com (a commercial proxy/scraping vendor) and firecrawl.dev — a direct competitor that is itself a candidate ranked 3rd in the same shortlist — and the refuter showed the underlying figure is no longer in the upstream README at all. Judge 1's own limits already name Firecrawl, Bright Data, TinyFish, Spider and Respan as commercially interested sources. The blind web modality's 15 queries are roundup-shaped ('best open source X 2026', 'state of the art Y'), which is the query form most likely to return vendor comparison pages.

Unverifiable star signal on a component that is simultaneously a catalog selection and a blind shortlist entry. headroomlabs-ai/headroom carries 73,422 stars on a repository created 2026-01-07; the discovery modality flagged this as a possible star-inflation signal, and BOTH judges independently reported that the GitHub stargazers endpoint returned HTTP 404 for every repository attempted in their environments (judge 1 verified against stanfordnlp/dspy and vercel-labs/agent-browser as controls), so no star-history or bot-detection check was run by anyone. Headroom is also in manifests/stack.json and named in the token-efficiency current_choice, so a star-driven blind shortlist and a catalog selection can appear to corroborate each other while neither has tested the signal.

The blind pass is catalog-blind but not domain-blind, and the domain framing shaped the scores. Judge 2's lens is explicitly 'research validity and task fit for US-equities R&D', and 'equities' appears 9 times and 'filings' 6 times in the sub-layer output. That framing produced real charges (Firecrawl and the browser agents penalised for live-only retrieval with no as-of snapshot; Headroom penalised for lossy statistical summarisation of numeric arrays) but it is a shared prior with the catalog, not an independent one. No repository-name leakage was found: grep of the sub-layer output returns zero occurrences of alpaca, nautilus, ibkr, rtk, repomix, ccusage, socraticode, jcodemunch, typesafe, qmd, beads or native-agent-stack; the single '<OPERATOR_HOME>' occurrence is judge 2's own blindness affirmation ('I opened no file under <OPERATOR_HOME> per the blindness rule').

Neither judge discovered anything — judge 1 states 'The shortlist was supplied, not discovered by me. I did not run an independent discovery sweep, so coverage gaps in the shortlist itself ... are not corrected by this judgment.' Only the refuter searched outside the supplied set, and it produced 6 alternatives of which 5 are absent from every catalog source. The judging stage therefore inherits and amplifies the discovery stage's biases rather than checking them; agreement between the two judges (identical #1 and #2) is agreement about a supplied list, not convergent discovery.

Catalog-side presence is not uniform, which can manufacture false 'absent from catalog' findings in either direction. repository-index.md has no row for microsoft/playwright or zizmorcore/zizmor even though both are in manifests/stack.json with pins, because the index is regenerated only 'from explicit source collections, not every repository URL mentioned in prose', and its main table is a frozen 2026-09-19 snapshot. Conversely the only 'Firecrawl' row is for firecrawl-mcp-server, so a prefix-matching check reports the engine as present when it is not. Every presence claim in this diff was therefore made with delimiter-anchored matching across repository-index.md, star-audit.json, landscape foundation.json, landscape us-equities.json, decision-index.json and manifests/stack.json together, not against the index alone.

Both catalogs and the blind pass over-weight the browser-automation slice relative to the sub-layer definition. Of the blind top 5 in each ranking, 3 of judge 1's and 3 of judge 2's are browser drivers or browser agents; the catalog's web-research selection is likewise 2 browser tools plus 2 search/literature clients. Token efficiency reached the judges through exactly one candidate (Headroom) and evaluation through effectively none, yet both are named thirds of the same sub-layer.
limits: Read-only pass. No command in this analysis was an acceptance check: every derivation came from jq/grep/python over the two supplied scratchpad JSON inputs and the two checked-out catalog repositories. I ran no gh api call, installed nothing, executed none of the 56 candidate repositories, and verified none of the blind pass's own gh api figures (stars, pushed_at, licences, commit counts, Scorecard values, arXiv abstract text, leaderboard CSV contents) against upstream. Everything attributed to the blind pass is quoted evidence from that pass, not independently confirmed fact.

Presence and absence claims are string-matching results over a fixed file set, not catalog semantics. Strict matching used 'github.com/<owner>/<repo>' followed by a delimiter, case-normalised, across catalogs/us-equities/repository-index.md, star-audit.json, decision-index.json, the us-equities *.md layer tables, catalogs/landscape/foundation.json, catalogs/landscape/us-equities.json and manifests/stack.json in both repositories. A repository recorded under a different owner, an alias, or only inside a nested supplement registered by JSON pointer could still be missed; I checked known renames explicitly (chopratejas/headroom, explodinggradients/ragas, Codium-ai/pr-agent, zizmor-rs/zizmor) but the set of renames I knew to check is not exhaustive.

The three catalog layers are foundation-catalog layers, so catalogs/us-equities/*.md layer tables cover different layers (data, engines, agents-operations) and are not the disposition source for web-research / token-efficiency / quality-evaluation. Dispositions for these three come from catalogs/landscape/foundation.json, star-audit.json, repository-index.md and manifests/stack.json. I did not read catalogs/landscape/candidate-quality-review.json (120 KB) or upstream-snapshot.json (245 KB) directly and relied on the wf1 layer records' quoted values for freshness_flags, corrections and overturn_when; if those extracts are themselves wrong, my freshness-related findings inherit the error. The wf1 records do carry their own 'verdict: corrected' status, which is why I quoted their correction text rather than their original extract.

I did not verify that the wf1 freshness snapshot predates the blind pass's 2026-09-21/22 reads. The Headroom pin finding (stack.json 0.37.0 and 'selected_version_matches_latest_stable' vs blind latest_release v0.38.0) is consistent with either a stale snapshot or a release published between the two reads; distinguishing them needs a fresh `gh api repos/headroomlabs-ai/headroom/releases/latest` plus the snapshot's own checked_at timestamp, which I did not run.

Score sums in blind_top are my arithmetic over the six per-criterion integers each judge recorded. Both judges explicitly declined to aggregate ('no averages, totals or cross-repository aggregates were computed'), so the sums are a reading convenience for this diff and carry no authority; the per-criterion values are the evidence.

No acceptance command was run for any recommended action, and none of the comparisons named in recommended_catalog_actions has been executed. Every 'keep-but-compare' disposition I propose is a labelling recommendation pending the comparison quoted from the layer's own overturn_when or next_action; none of them is supported yet.

Coverage of blind_found_absent_from_catalog is bounded by what the blind pass shortlisted or ranked, plus the refuter's 6 alternatives. The 34 merged candidates that were neither shortlisted nor judged (SeleniumHQ/selenium, semgrep/semgrep, confident-ai/deepeval, stanford-crfm/helm, truera/trulens, Giskard-AI/giskard-oss, evidentlyai/evidently, open-compress/claw-compactor and others) are mostly also absent from the catalog; I did not enumerate them as findings because no judge or refuter evidence exists to justify a row, but that is a scoping choice, not a determination that they are correctly excluded.

I could not test the one hypothesis that would most change the star-anchoring reading: whether the top-12-by-stars shortlist rule was specified by the workflow or chosen by the merit stage. The merit stage's limits do not state the rule; I inferred it by sorting the 46 merit rows and observing the cut falls exactly at rank 12, corroborated by the playwright-mcp row's own note.
