bias_observations: Decisive star anchoring in the blind shortlist. The 12-repo shortlist is an exact top-12-by-stars cut of the surviving candidates: the lowest shortlisted star count is Trivy at 38,000 and the highest non-shortlisted, non-dropped candidate is sgl-project/sglang at 36,282 - no candidate below 38,000 was shortlisted and none above it was omitted. Computed from merit.rows/merit.shortlist/merit.dropped in the F-ops record. The judged 'merit' therefore ranks a star-selected pool, not the candidate space.

That cut removed essentially the entire catalog-selected set before judging: restic 36,172, gitleaks 29,419, grafana/loki 28,930, anchore/grype 12,913, open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector 7,581, zizmorcore/zizmor 6,551, sigstore/cosign 6,317 and dagucloud/dagu all fell below the 38,000 line despite being in merged[]. The blind pass then compared the catalog's lane only against heavyweight general infrastructure.

The refuter's 'better alternatives' are a near-perfect re-derivation of the existing catalog. All five - anchore/grype, restic/restic, open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector, zizmorcore/zizmor, sigstore/cosign - already carry catalog rows or stack.json ids (grype agents-operations default; restic recovery-portability selected at the identical 0.19.1; otel-collector observation-inference selected; zizmor ci-supply-chain selected at the identical 1.30.1; cosign agents-operations conditional). A catalog-free pass converging on the catalog's own selections is genuine independent corroboration, but it also means the refuter stage - not the judge stage - is where this sub-layer's blind signal actually lives.

The engineering judge disclosed the bias itself: 'The shortlist was supplied pre-filtered; I ran no independent discovery pass, so absent categories are unexamined rather than rejected', and then enumerated OpenTelemetry Collector, Loki, Tempo, Jaeger, VictoriaMetrics, SigNoz, restic, borgbackup, Dagster, Prefect, Temporal, systemd timers, zizmor, semgrep, grype, syft, scorecard-action, cosign and LiteLLM as missing, closing with 'No conclusion here should be read as these twelve are the best available.' The rankings should be read with that caveat attached.

Scorecard availability is confounded with repository type, not quality. The OpenSSF Scorecard API returned HTTP 404 for five of twelve shortlisted repos (uptime-kuma, ollama, vllm, llama.cpp, LocalAI) - all the local-inference and self-hosted-app entries. Provenance comparisons are therefore valid only among the seven with records, which systematically advantages Go/CNCF infrastructure projects on the maintenance_provenance and evidence criteria. Trivy's Scorecard is additionally ~6 months staler (2026-03-16) than its peers (2026-09-14/21), so the Trivy-vs-grype Scorecard gap that drove the refuter's better-alternative finding is partly a snapshot-date artifact.

The engineering judge's headline SOTA claim for the #1 repo was itself a tooling artifact: the refuter found Prometheus was scanned with Scorecard v5.5.0 (which emits CI-Tests, Contributors, Vulnerabilities, Dependency-Update-Tool) while airflow, trivy, rclone, grafana and netdata were scanned with v5.5.1-0.20260908181711 (which does not). Cross-repo Scorecard comparison in this sub-layer is not like-for-like.

A mechanical licence rule dropped 15 of 17 candidates on GitHub's spdx_id=NOASSERTION alone - including borg, localstack, litellm, SigNoz, windmill, n8n, sigstore-python, in-toto and slsa. The merit stage flagged this honestly as 'a detection gap in GitHub's API, not a determination that no license exists', but the effect is real: borgbackup (restic's only serious peer) and sigstore-python and in-toto (core supply-chain provenance) were removed before any judging, biasing the surviving pool toward projects GitHub happens to auto-classify.

An awesome-list repository, samber/awesome-prometheus-alerts, entered the candidate pool as a candidate tool rather than as a source - echo-chamber contamination at the discovery layer. It was removed at the licence step, incidentally rather than on category grounds.

No Alpaca, NautilusTrader, IBKR or other north-star name appears anywhere in this sub-layer's 85 merged candidates, 12-repo shortlist, judge scores or refuter output, and the 23 recorded queries are all generic ops phrasing. For F-ops specifically, the blindness rule held.

Catalog-side bias runs the other way: three of the nine observation-inference selections (AgentsView 0.43.0, otel-tui 0.7.5, Claude HUD 0.8.0) are small agent-specific tools that no star-thresholded discovery pass can reach, and two of them carry no source_pin. They may well be right for this stack, but they are structurally immune to the kind of external corroboration this exercise provides.

Four of the six layers carry three or more selections with contradictory or split dispositions across the landscape JSON and the us-equities markdown (grype unqualified/default, sglang unqualified/alternative, vLLM measured_tradeoff/default, Prefect and Dagster conditional/alternative). Where a repository has two dispositions, any coverage comparison can select whichever one supports its conclusion.

residual_bias: Star cut: binding in 6 of 10 sub-layers, and in 5 of those the 12-repo shortlist is EXACTLY the top 12 by star count among rule-passing candidates - T-engines 32 passers to 12 (12/12 overlap), T-strategies 17 to 12 (12/12), F-retrieval-memory 33 to 12 (12/12), F-research-efficiency 46 to 12 (12/12), F-ops 68 to 12 (12/12); T-data 32 to 12 at 10/12. In T-runtimes, T-alpaca-org and F-agents the passer set was already exactly 12, so the star cut was vacuous there and the licence/staleness drop rules did the selecting instead (48 of 60, 56 of 68 and 28 of 40 dropped). Several bias sections generalise 'star anchoring is structural' across all ten sub-layers; that is measurably wrong for three of them and misidentifies the mechanism.

Judge rankings are not a reliable merit signal: 44 of 100 SOTA claims were refuted, and 18 repositories have claims with zero surviving verdict, including both claims for several top-ranked repos (OpenHands ranked #1 by one judge with both claims refuted; playwright #1 by both judges with both refuted; faiss #1 by one judge with both refuted; qlib, questdb, duckdb, trivy, airflow, llama.cpp, rclone likewise). Any recommendation that cites a ranking rather than a surviving verdict is resting on an overturned signal.

Merit-metadata corruption biases any mechanical re-ranking: 115 of 514 rows are missing a core field, and the open_issues field is defective in 97 rows including all 68 of T-alpaca-org. has_tests is independently known wrong for langgraph, alpaca-trade-api-go, alpaca-trade-api-csharp, d-e-s-o/apca, polars and nautilus_trader. The has_tests/has_ci columns are root-directory-listing heuristics and must not be used as evidence.

Name leakage into the 'blind' pass is documented and direct in four sub-layers: T-engines (gh api orgs/nautechsystems, orgs/QuantConnect, orgs/alpacahq, orgs/quantopian plus seeded 'nautilus trader' and 'lean algorithmic trading engine' searches), T-runtimes, T-data ('gh api orgs/alpacahq/repos --paginate', 'nautilus trader data catalog parquet github') and T-alpaca-org (nautilus_trader ranked FIRST in the merit shortlist of an Alpaca sub-layer on the strength of an open RFC issue). The catalog/blind convergence on NautilusTrader, LEAN and alpaca-py therefore carries much less independent weight than an unseeded sweep. T-strategies, F-agents and F-ops report clean greps for north-star names, so the leakage is not uniform.

Mechanical licence gating on GitHub's spdx_id is a detector artifact that systematically removed on-topic candidates before judging, and the catalog repeatedly holds better licence evidence than the blind pass: Serena (the catalog's code-navigation default), pgvector, Weaviate, Arize-ai/phoenix (catalog records Elastic-2.0), langfuse (catalog records MIT core plus ee), openai/evals, the entire QuickFIX family, borgbackup, sigstore-python, in-toto, OpenBB, vectorbt, rqalpha and pybroker were all dropped on NOASSERTION alone. In F-research-efficiency and F-ops this removed the whole dedicated-eval and FIX-engine categories before any judge saw them.

Catalog-side coverage asymmetry: engines-strategies absorbs 5 of the 10 blind sub-layers while 17 of 20 layers are covered by exactly one, so no layer except engines-strategies, agents-operations and data-research has independent cross-sub-layer corroboration. Catalog-side discovery is also star-shaped - repository-index.md's Discovery column has only 'Starred' and 'Beyond stars' values and is built on a 342-repository personal star snapshot (catalogs/convergence-practice/public-starred.json), which structurally hides small purpose-built tooling (Worktrunk, sandbox-runtime, jCodeMunch, QMD, ai-memory, AgentsView, otel-tui, Claude HUD) from any external corroboration.

Catalog records required correction in 19 of 20 layers (verdict=corrected; only instructions-skills is 'confirmed'), with 80 discrepancies and 116 corrections recorded. Cross-family agreement is absent for 7 of 20 layers (codex=diverge on workers, isolation, token-efficiency, quality-evaluation, foundation-memory, agents-operations; codex=unknown on data-research). Internal disposition splits produce false disagreement signals in any automated diff: grype unqualified/default, sglang unqualified/alternative, vLLM measured_tradeoff/default, lean-alpaca Default/conditional, nautilus_trader alternative-in-index/selected-in-manifest, anthropics/skills overlap-in-foundation/selected-in-closure-doc.

Both sides are documentary. No judge and no catalog card in this diff rests on executed code, a reproduced benchmark or a measured numeric result; the only genuinely measured comparators in the entire run are OpenSSF Scorecard values and the catalog's own TOON measured_comparison and skfolio native_proven receipts. Agreement between two documentary passes that share a domain prior (both judge lenses are explicitly US-equities-framed, and star-audit.md states 'These choices are conditioned on the existing LEAN research-first and Alpaca-paper direction') is not corroboration.
